```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

import pypanelsim as pps
```

## Build one small design from each project

The examples use interactive sample sizes. Increase only the configuration
dimensions to run the paper-scale law.

```{python}
simulators = {
    "Lepskii tensor blocks": pps.lepskii_design(
        "tensor_blocks",
        config=pps.LepskiiPanelConfig(n_units=240),
    ),
    "ATT-DML nonlinear CPT": pps.att_dml_design(
        "conditional_parallel_trends_nonlinear",
        config=pps.ATTDMConditionalConfig(
            n_units=240,
            n_features=10,
            n_active=3,
            trend_strength=2.0,
        ),
    ),
    "Regression compression": pps.regression_compression_design(
        config=pps.RegressionCompressionConfig(
            n_units=240,
            n_periods=35,
            adoption_period=15,
            n_treated=100,
            effect_profile="concave",
        )
    ),
    "gsynth2 composite": pps.gsynth_composite_design(
        config=pps.GSynthCompositeConfig(
            n_control=160,
            n_treated=40,
            n_pre=30,
            n_post=8,
        )
    ),
}

panels = {
    label: simulator.simulate(streams=pps.SimulationSeeds.from_seed(42))
    for label, simulator in simulators.items()
}
```

Every result has the same wide and long interchange contract.

```{python}
pd.DataFrame(
    [
        {
            "design": label,
            "units": panel.n_units,
            "periods": panel.n_periods,
            "cohorts": np.unique(
                panel.adoption_times[panel.ever_treated]
            ).size,
            "true ATT": panel.true_att,
            "covariates": panel.unit_covariates.shape[1],
        }
        for label, panel in panels.items()
    ]
).round(3)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-research-suite-panels
#| fig-cap: "Observed outcomes and treatment masks from four downstream research designs."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 12

figure, axes = plt.subplots(4, 2, figsize=(12, 12), constrained_layout=True)
for row, (label, panel) in enumerate(panels.items()):
    order = np.argsort(panel.adoption_times, kind="stable")
    outcome_image = axes[row, 0].matshow(
        panel.outcome[order], aspect="auto", cmap="coolwarm"
    )
    axes[row, 1].matshow(
        panel.treatment[order], aspect="auto", cmap="Greys", vmin=0, vmax=1
    )
    axes[row, 0].set_title(f"{label}: observed outcome")
    axes[row, 1].set_title(f"{label}: treatment")
    axes[row, 0].set_ylabel("unit")
    figure.colorbar(outcome_image, ax=axes[row, 0], fraction=0.03)
    for axis in axes[row]:
        axis.set_xlabel("period")
plt.show()
```

## Inspect support-aware truth

The Lepskii draft targets event times from $-5$ through $12$. Late positive
event times are not observed for every cohort. The truth object changes the
target population only when support changes.

```{python}
lepskii_truth = panels["Lepskii tensor blocks"].truth.event_study(
    event_times=range(-5, 13)
)
pd.DataFrame(dict(lepskii_truth)).round(3)
```

The ATT-DML example has two periods and one treated period. Its raw ten-column
covariate matrix is estimator visible. Assignment and outcomes used the
thirteen-column expanded basis. The reported ATT is the realized mean of the
Gaussian treatment-effect shocks, not the configured population mean.

```{python}
att_panel = panels["ATT-DML nonlinear CPT"]
{
    "estimator_covariates": att_panel.unit_covariates.shape,
    "internal_covariates": att_panel.metadata["assignment"]["coefficients"].shape,
    "assignment_active_features": att_panel.metadata["assignment"][
        "active_features"
    ],
    "true_att": att_panel.true_att,
}
```

## Hand off to an estimator

The simulator does not choose an estimand or estimator.

```{python}
panel = panels["gsynth2 composite"]
y, w = panel.as_arrays(copy=True)
long_columns = panel.as_long_dict(
    include_effect_surface=True,
    include_annotations=True,
)

y.shape, w.shape, tuple(long_columns)[:8]
```
